newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN SHARE RECOVERY HOPES DASHED BY U.S. DATA.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN SHARE RECOVERY HOPES DASHED BY U.S. DATA.

text.p: Hope that U.S. jobs data on Friday would rekindle Belgium's equity rally were dashed when initial optimism about the figures evaporated in late trade.
The Bel-20 leading share index ended up 1.41 points, or 0.07 percent, at 2,080.67 points with 13 issues higher, five lower and two unchanged.

The index peaked at 2,093.20 points as investors welcomed news the headline March non-farm payrolls number came in at a lower-than-expected 175,000. But as bond markets zoomed in on news that average earnings had risen the sentiment turned.
"It looks bearish for next week," one trader said.

Wall Street stocks moved sharply lower at the start of trade in New York, which came after the Belgian market closed, he noted. "Good Friday was last week. This week it could be black Friday," he said.
Retailers were Friday's biggest losers, with Delhaize falling 5.46 percent to 1,730 francs and GIB slipping 2.50 percent to 1,560 francs.

Delhaize had been under pressure all day after its U.S. Food Lion unit had lost ground earlier in the week, but fell sharply in late trade when it emerged several U.S. brokerages had downgraded Food Lion shares, dealers said.
Food Lion said late on Thursday that first quarter 1997 earnings rose 11 percent, but growth had been slowed by its acquisition last year of the U.S. Kash 'n Karry chain.
Dealers said GIB's move lower was a technical reaction to gains it made on Thursday in an otherwise downward market.

However, financials -- with the exception of Dexia CC -- were firm. Generale Bank rose 100 francs to 13,300 francs. Kredietbank was up 150 francs at 12,250 francs. BBL was up 80 francs at 7,490 francs and insurers Fortis AG and Royale Belge both added 10 francs. -- Nick Antonovics, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6817, Fax +32 2 230 7710
